title: Right move away from the boundary
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a position in the range of $n+2$ positions with $p\ne n+1$. Moving $p$ by $1$ with clamping gives the position $p+1$.
hypotheses_covered: A position p in the range of n + 2 positions
replaced:
Let $p$ be an input-head position on an input of length $n$ with $p \ne n + 1$. Then the
clamped move of $p$ by the sign $1$ is exactly the position $p + 1$: a right move that
does not start at the right boundary increments the position.
